trust_decision.summary: With ownPropertyOnly, template reads of scope data may return only own properties; Context.readProperty enforces it via readJSProperty, but array reads by negative index and .first/.last (and the first/last filters) skip that check and return prototype-inherited indices.

landing_point.why: The summary names the negative index and .first/.last. All of these are in Context.readProperty, which sits right next to the existing readJSProperty ownPropertyOnly check.

fix_sites.entry_point: template property access {{ a[-1] }} / {{ a[i] }}; public Context.getSync/_get API
readFirst/readLast helpers reached from {{ a.first }} / {{ a.last }} and from map/sort/sum property paths

fix_sites.module_kind: builtin filter module (separate implementation of first/last)
builtin filter module (switched to Array.prototype.join.call; same inherited-index semantics)

fix_sites.entry_point: new helper readArrayElement inserted here (fix.diff:171-175), used by the context and filter sites

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/filters/array.ts:15-16 (first/last filters reimplement element reads with v[0] / util last(), src/util/underscore.ts:120-124, outside Context and with no access to ownPropertyOnly unless they switch to a this-bound FilterImpl)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The pinned docs say ownPropertyOnly is 'a read policy for scope data—not a sandbox for filters, tags' (docs/source/tutorials/security-model.md:65), so filters and the for/tablerow/render iteration can be argued out of scope. The published fix even writes that exception into the option doc (fix.diff:156-159).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Must keep working: {{ a.size }} still returns length for sparse or polluted arrays; arr[-1] and arr | first/last on real arrays and on strings (isArrayLike strings); Drop objects still read through their prototype chain; ownPropertyOnly:false still follows normal JS lookup. An over-broad fix (e.g. dropping holes, returning '' for strings, or applying hasOwnProperty to Drops) breaks these.

first / last filters on arrays and array-likes (src/filters/array.ts:15-16)
filter result stored via assign then output (fix.diff:216)

j.j_sites_touched: src/context/context.ts, src/filters/array.ts, src/util/underscore.ts (plus src/liquid-options.ts doc comment)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap the negative-index line in Context.readProperty and readFirst/readLast to readJSProperty / a hasOwnProperty check, and leave the first/last filters and every iteration route alone.

out_of_scope_notes: findScope uses `key in candidate`, which includes prototype keys, to choose the top-level scope (src/context/context.ts:116-123); this concerns object keys, not array indices, so it was not pursued.
unverified: The fix's join/compact/concat/slice/where changes (fix.diff:97,115,123,133-134,143) appear behaviour-neutral for inherited indices, because Array.prototype.X.call still reads through the prototype. So the advisory's join/slice/compact claims are probably still open after the fix. Not run.

Fairness risk: the advisory summary lists for-loop iteration and reverse as bypasses, yet the upstream fix declines them and documents the exclusion (fix.diff:156-159), and the pinned docs already exclude filters and tags (docs/source/tutorials/security-model.md:65). A hidden test for O8 routes needs an explicit report requirement and a defined expected output (skip the hole? undefined?).

Behaviour change not covered by tests: a string key '-1' (e.g. {% assign i = '-1' %}{{ a[i] }}) used to read the last element via the `< 0` coercion at src/context/context.ts:128. After the fix, isNumber fails and readJSProperty returns undefined. This is a possible differential or regression test.
